name: Washington

creditorClaims.text: If notice is published, claims are barred unless presented within 4 months after first publication (or, for creditors given actual notice, the later of 30 days after notice or 4 months after publication); reasonably ascertainable creditors not given actual notice, and all creditors if no notice was given, have 24 months after death (RCW 11.40.051).

earliestClose.text: A personal representative with nonintervention powers closes the estate by filing a declaration of completion once claims are paid or disposed of and administration is complete (RCW 11.68.110); this follows the 4-month claims period of RCW 11.40.051.

smallEstate.text: Forty days after death, a successor may collect personal property by affidavit if the decedent's entire probate estate (excluding the surviving spouse's or domestic partner's community share), less liens and encumbrances, does not exceed $100,000 and no personal representative application is pending (RCW 11.62.010). Not indexed.

simplified.text: Affidavit procedure up to $100,000 (RCW 11.62.010); nonintervention probate closed by declaration of completion without court approval (RCW 11.68.110).

filingFee.text: In probate proceedings the party instituting them pays $200 when filing the first document (RCW 36.18.020(2)(f)); counties may add local surcharges.

personalRepFee.text: Absent a will provision, the personal representative receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210).

attorneyFee.text: An attorney performing services for the estate receives compensation the court deems just and reasonable (RCW 11.48.210); fees paid must be disclosed in the declaration of completion (RCW 11.68.110).

uncertain: Effective date of the $100,000 affidavit limit not shown (smallEstate.effective = null).
